decisions.reason: As a relatively generic utility web service with limited strategic importance to the firm's energy-focused platform, it is easier to discontinue if uptake has been weak despite the modest public launch commitment.

This database is close to the firm's core data business, so prior development effort and the wish to justify expansion into adjacent regulated-market content make continued support more likely than withdrawal.
The service fits the firm's core competence in regulated energy calculations and process support, which encourages management to persist and fold it into the broader SaaS platform direction.
An end-customer tariff database builds directly on the firm's database and analytics strengths, so sunk development effort and strategic fit favor keeping it unless failure is unmistakable.
Custom web services align well with the firm's stated move toward modular SaaS and broader end-to-end service provision, making management inclined to continue rather than retreat.

A postal code lookup service is a low-differentiation add-on with comparatively low sunk cost and weak centrality to the firm's announced energy-platform trajectory, so it is the easiest product to remove.
